subject.title: Transcript redaction corrupts Anthropic/Bedrock reasoning signatures (AIza/LTAI false positive), causing persistent replay_invalid

question: Should OpenClaw preserve structurally valid Anthropic/Bedrock provider signature fields even when their opaque bytes contain credential-shaped substrings, and should existing ellipsis-poisoned signatures be repaired by dropping the signature or thinking block?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the permanent fix must choose a redaction boundary that protects provider replay bytes without letting real credentials bypass transcript redaction.

options.title: Field-scoped signature preservation
options.body: Preserve validated opaque replay tokens only in known provider signature fields, and add focused repair coverage for already-redacted signature values.

options.title: Pattern-only hardening
options.body: Make vendor token patterns stricter or case-sensitive while keeping the current redaction-idempotency requirement, accepting that other false positives may still corrupt signatures.

options.title: Send-side guard only
options.body: Drop ellipsis-marked or invalid Bedrock/Anthropic signatures before replay, preventing provider 400s but leaving upstream transcript corruption possible.

recommendation.title: Field-scoped signature preservation
recommendation.body: Preserve validated opaque replay tokens only in known provider signature fields, and add focused repair coverage for already-redacted signature values.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame points to vincentkoc for the active redaction and Bedrock replay surfaces, making them the best available routing owner for the security-boundary choice.
